technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring for Apache Kafka to implement Kafka-related features (concurrency, compression, ACK, batching).
Leverage Spring Integration's Kafka support for bindRequestor and bindReplier implementations.
Integrate Sqoop via command-line interface (CLI) for job management (stop, logs, incremental load).
Use SLF4J with Logback for logging and stream Sqoop logs to the application's logging system.
Implement global configuration defaults with per-deployment overrides using Spring's @ConfigurationProperties.
assumptions: Existing Kafka and Sqoop integrations are partially in place in the codebase.
The development team has prior experience with Spring Framework, Kafka, and Sqoop.
CI/CD pipeline is already configured for automated builds and testing.
Logging infrastructure (e.g., ELK stack) is available for streaming Sqoop logs.
Sqoop jobs are managed via CLI commands and can be controlled programmatically.

activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance tests for Kafka message bus integration, including test environment setup and CI pipeline integration.
Add configuration options for Kafka producer/consumer concurrency and compression, with global defaults and per-deployment overrides.
Implement acknowledgment options for Kafka producers to guarantee message delivery success.
Implement Spring Integration bindings for Kafka producers expecting async replies and consumers handling requests with replies.
Add options for Kafka producer batching to ingest data in batches instead of payload-at-a-time.
Implement functionality to stop an existing Sqoop job programmatically for resource cleanup.
Capture and stream Sqoop job logs to the application's logging mechanism for troubleshooting.
Configure Sqoop to perform incremental imports based on a timestamp or ID column for new data retrieval.
